evidence.title: X-Men: The Official Game
evidence.text: X-Men: The Official Game (also known as X3: The Official Game) is Activision's tie-in video game to the 2006 film "".

evidence.title: X-Men: The Official Game
evidence.text: The game covers the events of the films "X2" and "", specifically following the characters of Wolverine, Iceman, and Nightcrawler.

evidence.title: X-Men: The Official Game
evidence.text: It also bridges the gap between the two films, explaining why Nightcrawler is not present for "The Last Stand", and also introduces new foes to the "X-Men" film canon, such as HYDRA.

evidence.title: Mighty Max (toyline)
evidence.text: Mighty Max was a series of toys that were manufactured by Bluebird Toys PLC in the UK in 1992, and designed by Big Monster Toys.

evidence.title: Mighty Max (toyline)
evidence.text: The toys were similar to the earlier Polly Pocket toyline; however, these toys were marketed primarily towards young boys.

evidence.title: Mighty Max (toyline)
evidence.text: In Canada and the USA, they were distributed by Irwin Toy Limited and Mattel Inc. respectively.

evidence.title: Mighty Max (toyline)
evidence.text: The original toyline consisted mainly of "Doom Zones" and "Horror Heads."

evidence.title: Mighty Max (toyline)
evidence.text: "Doom Zones" were small playsets with a horror theme and featured miniature figurines of menacing creatures and the hero Max, a young boy with blond hair, jeans, a white t-shirt with a red "M" on it, and a baseball cap (the color varied based on the playset purchased) which also always had an "M" on it.

evidence.title: Mighty Max (toyline)
evidence.text: The "Horror Heads" were smaller-sized playsets, also shaped like the heads of creatures and contained miniature figures.

evidence.title: Mighty Max (toyline)
evidence.text: It was later adapted into a TV series, as well as a tie-in video game produced by Ocean Software for the Super NES and Mega Drive/Genesis.
